candidates.question: A DAB GraphQL entity maps a SQL Server 2022 table's UnitCost DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL to cost and AvailableUnits INT NOT NULL to available. Its published filter schema accepts unquoted integer literals for both fields' gt inputs. A client needs cost > 100 and available > 0, in pages of 25. A response contains hasNextPage = true and an opaque endCursor. Permissions and entity configuration are valid. Select two client behaviors that filter and continue the query.

answerChoices.text: Filter using UnitCost and AvailableUnits because those are the physical database column names.
Use filter: { cost: { gt: 100 }, available: { gt: 0 } }.
Request first: 25 again without after, treating the row limit as an advance instruction.
Use the returned endCursor as after, retaining the same filter and first: 25.

candidates.explanation: Apply the numeric gt filters to the exposed field names, then continue using the returned cursor.
candidates.deepExplanation: The numeric SQL columns and explicit GraphQL input contract support the unquoted integer literals in the offered filter; aliases or column names alone would not establish that compatibility. Treat the cursor as opaque and retain the filter and page-size criteria when continuing. This does not promise a transactionally frozen result across requests or that every remaining page contains 25 rows.

whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.a: Physical names would be appropriate if exposed unchanged. The training says clients use mapped/exposed names, so these internal names do not match the stated GraphQL contract.
whyOtherAnswersAreWrong.c: first controls page size. Omitting after is appropriate for the initial page or restarting the result set, not advancing after the page already received.
